name: Welford online central second moment
definition: For a finite sequence initialize k=1, m_1=x_1, M_1=0; for k≥2 set δ=x_k−m_(k−1), m_k=m_(k−1)+δ/k, M_k=M_(k−1)+δ(x_k−m_k). Return M_k=Σ_(i=1)^k(x_i−m_k)² in exact arithmetic
variables: k positive count; x_k observation; m_k running mean; M_k unnormalized second central moment
assumptions: Nonempty finite real observations with consistent units; exact count, valid arithmetic, and representable intermediates for a floating-point implementation; no independence assumption for descriptive moments
limitations: Rounded mean updates may stagnate and subtraction or products may overflow or underflow; results depend on order in floating point; unbiased sample variance additionally needs independent identically distributed observations of finite variance
failure_conditions: Empty input, nonfinite values, count overflow or nonfinite intermediate
computation: Initialize directly from the first value; update the mean before using the new mean in the central-moment correction. Use M_k/k for the empirical variance and M_k/(k−1) for sample variance when k≥2; retain count and reject invalid numerical states.

source.citation: Pébay (2008), Formulas for Robust, One-Pass Parallel Computation of Covariances and Arbitrary-Order Statistical Moments, SAND2008-6212, pp. 7–8, eqs. (1.1)–(1.2), citing Welford (1962). DOI 10.2172/1028931. https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc837537/m2/1/high_res_d/1028931.pdf

application: General streaming numerical summary; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite numeric observations and declared arithmetic.
incompatible_methods: Treating a rounded accumulator as exact
mechanism_note: Recenter the first k−1 observations by m_(k−1)−m_k; the cross term vanishes because their old centered deviations sum to zero. Their correction plus the new squared deviation equals δ(x_k−m_k). This updates a centered second moment in constant state, unlike the registered summation, conditional-variance and raw scatter methods; not a guarantee of floating-point exactness.

name: Chan pairwise central second moment merge
definition: For nonempty disjoint blocks A,B set n=n_A+n_B, δ=m_B−m_A, m=m_A+δ n_B/n, M=M_A+M_B+δ² n_A n_B/n
variables: n_A,n_B positive block counts; m_A,m_B block means; M_A,M_B block unnormalized second central moments; n,m,M combined state
assumptions: Disjoint observation-index blocks with finite values in common units and internally consistent moment states; counts exact and required intermediates representable; identities in real arithmetic
limitations: Merge order, large count imbalance, squared differences and finite precision can change rounded results or overflow; no universal accuracy guarantee or independence inference
failure_conditions: Nonpositive or inconsistent counts, overlapping observation indices, nonfinite state or intermediate
Sample variance requested for total count below two
computation: Represent empty blocks separately: skip an empty block, reject two empty blocks for a mean or variance query. For two nonempty blocks combine counts, mean and between-block correction; choose a fixed merge tree for reproducibility. Return M/n or M/(n−1) for n≥2 as appropriate.

source.citation: Pébay (2008), SAND2008-6212, p. 8, eqs. (1.3)–(1.4), attributing the block formula to Chan, Golub and LeVeque (1979). DOI 10.2172/1028931. https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc837537/m2/1/high_res_d/1028931.pdf

application: General parallel numerical summary; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Two finite valid disjoint block moment states.
incompatible_methods: Merging overlapping observations as independent blocks
mechanism_note: Within each block the deviations about its own mean sum to zero; shifting the block centers adds n_A(m_A−m)²+n_B(m_B−m)²=δ² n_A n_B/n. A singleton B gives the Welford correction. Arbitrary block merging adds parallel aggregation capability, but the shared recentering identity warrants variant classification.
